description:
## Mandatory context and boundaries
Read the parent epic first. Applicable owners: AGENTS.md; docs/agent-tools.md; docs/WORKFLOW_AGENT.md; docs/exec-plans/PLAN_STRATEGY.md; docs/action-reuse.md; docs/testing-approach.md; docs/services/channels.md (communication/Jido bridge and provider contracts); docs/services/engine.md (history, admission, finalization and delivery). Read docs/documentation.md before documentation/skill edits, docs/services/system-config.md before credential fixtures, and local module @moduledoc before extending a helper. Apply code-quality for code and skill-creator for the skill.
Only test/ additions or backward-compatible support changes, lib/mix/tasks/zaq.test.gen.channel.ex, and .agents/skills/add-channel-integration-tests/** are authorized. Do not edit application modules, dependency source/pins, config, migrations, mix.exs, CI, or unrelated skills. Existing-test expectation changes require the testing handbook's explicit approval; this epic authorizes additive coverage, not changing expectations.
Use real bridges, NodeRouter, Engine admission/history/persistence and configured Agent execution. Only provider/LLM boundaries are faked. A production defect is a reported blocker with a reproducer; do not patch production, silently omit a scenario, weaken an assertion, or close the issue as complete.
Validation timing, failure handling and final gates are owned by docs/WORKFLOW_AGENT.md. Record executed commands/results in this issue. No new browser E2E is needed: this work adds test/developer infrastructure without changing a deployed UI journey. No commit/push/merge authorization is implied.

Parent epic: zaq-o9d

## Functional specification and files
Implement Mix.Tasks.Zaq.Test.Gen.Channel in lib/mix/tasks/zaq.test.gen.channel.ex. It is the only allowed new non-test Elixir implementation file. Keep generation logic in this module (private cohesive helpers); do not add test/support/channels/integration/generator.ex that would be unavailable in :dev and do not modify mix.exs.
Own templates test/support/channels/integration/templates/driver.ex.eex and provider_test.exs.eex, and tests test/mix/tasks/zaq_test_gen_channel_test.exs.
CLI: mix zaq.test.gen.channel <provider> --adapter <Elixir.Module> [--dry-run].
Exactly one lowercase snake_case provider matching ^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*$ and a fully qualified alias are required. Reject unknown/duplicate flags, invalid/missing identifiers, path separators/traversal and extra positional args. No --force or arbitrary --output. A production adapter must already be available: compile needed production modules using Mix's normal task path without app.start, then verify core adapter identity/transform/send callbacks. If unavailable/incompatible, fail clearly with zero writes; do not edit dependencies or install Teams.
The task must run in the default dev environment without loading test-support modules or starting ZAQ/Repo/listeners/agents. Existing deps/compilation prerequisites may be needed, but no running database/provider is needed.
Outputs for teams:
- test/support/channels/integration/drivers/teams.ex defining Drivers.Teams and @behaviour Driver, all six callback stubs with explicit provider-specific failures, native-message/script/delivery TODO guidance.
- test/zaq/channels/integration/providers/teams_test.exs defining provider-specific contract assertions with an explicit unfinished implementation failure. The template can use Integration.Case with a driver: option; Case must support this documented usage.
- Exactly one sorted teams: Drivers.Teams entry inside registry.ex's dedicated markers.
Do not generate or claim a production adapter, change production provider config, silently omit registration, or insert skipped/pending tests. Generated stubs should compile when the adapter is available, but fail tests until actually implemented.
Registry editing must not execute test source; use the unique literal marker block plus AST validation for syntactic/shape integrity. Preserve everything outside the owned block. Validate final generated Elixir syntax before writes.
--dry-run prints planned new paths plus the registry diff, with byte-for-byte zero changes. Normal execution preflights every path/registration/marker, rejects existing files and any symlink escape from test/, stages all output, verifies the registry was not concurrently changed, and rolls back only its own writes if a later commit fails. Never overwrite unrelated files. Repeat invocation fails with actionable existing-integration guidance and no modifications.

## Tests to add before implementation
- Valid installed/synthetic adapter: expected two files plus one sorted registration; generated code parses/compiles and contains executable failing stubs, not silent skips.
- Default dev task loading works without test-support compiled; no application/Repo/provider process startup occurs.
- Missing adapter/module/callback, malformed provider/module, unknown/duplicate flags, absent/duplicate registry markers, duplicate provider, existing target, symlink/path escape: zero writes.
- Dry-run with valid and invalid inputs: exact no-change assertions.
- Later-write failure and concurrent registry edit: preserve original/unrelated files; clean up only owned output.
- Deterministic output, sorted entries and provider-name/path containment property tests using existing libraries.
- A valid generated registration is discovered by the same all-driver matrix; incomplete callbacks produce visible failure. Tests use disposable project roots/fixtures and Mix shell capture, never the real checkout or an actual Teams dependency/account.
Do not assert giant template snapshots when parsing generated modules and testing observable behavior is sufficient.

## Branches/paths validated
Success/dry-run, input/adapter validation, existing destination/registration, malformed registry, filesystem failures, rollback, default-env loading and incomplete scaffold detection.

## Mocking plan
No provider or LLM network is required for generator tests. Test adapters/filesystem roots are local temporary fixtures. Do not stub the real generator logic or require external command/network access.

## Documentation
Task @moduledoc/help and test README own usage/output/error examples. Document production-adapter prerequisite and test-only output. Keep the exact command and callbacks consistent with templates.

## Action reuse assessment
Local-only developer filesystem operation. Existing lib/mix/tasks/hooks.verify.ex demonstrates compilation without app.start; other tasks generate unrelated fixtures or manage databases, so do not reuse their domain behaviour. No meaningful runtime/Jido Action consumer exists. Contract is validated CLI -> bounded test-file plan/write or error; idempotency is refusal on repeat. Verify via temp-project outcomes and no-start/no-outside-write assertions.

## Done when
Task works from default dev mode, creates exactly the documented scaffold/registration, rejects unsafe/partial inputs without collateral edits, all generator tests pass, and the actual repo remains within the explicit allowed paths.

comments.text: Implemented compile-only dev Mix task, two EEx templates and safe registry registration. Validates installed adapter callbacks, strict CLI identifiers/options, literal unique ordered markers, existing destinations, symlink containment and generated syntax. Dry-run has zero writes. Exclusive lock serializes generator writers; stale plans reject registry edits; staged registry replacement and owned-file rollback cover later failures. Generator validation: 1 property + 10 tests passed, including nested default-dev execution with no ZAQ/Repo startup or test-support loading. Generated fixture compiles and fails explicitly in unfinished callbacks; no Teams dependency installed. mix q passes. Action reuse: local-only developer filesystem operation; reused existing compile-only Mix-task pattern and shared test contract/templates, no domain Action added.
